title: M-IRT Novelty Positioning: Consistency Literature + Contamination Provenance
summary: Iter-2 research artifact for M-IRT that (i) verifies every arXiv ID and venue claim for the 12 cited references in the paper's Related Work section, (ii) adds a 'reference-free consistency as a research thread' section surveying Liu et al. 2024 (arXiv:2410.02205), Jang et al. 2022 BECEL, Novikova et al. 2025 (arXiv:2505.00268), ConsistencyGate 2026 (arXiv:2607.22962), Elazar et al. 2021 (arXiv:2102.01017), Musawi & Lu 2025 (arXiv:2505.08389), and Jang & Lukasiewicz 2023 (arXiv:2303.06273), and (iii) grounds the natural-contamination system-prompt-injection protocol in Sainz et al. (TS-Guessing), Xu et al. (contamination survey), and HELM. The deliverable contains a 12-row verification log, three distinguishing-M-IRT novelty bullets (polytomous vs binary, dynamic vs fixed, contamination-resistance vs robustness), and a drop-in 200-word citation paragraph for Section 2 of the paper.
answer: All 12 reviewer-named arXiv IDs and venue claims in the M-IRT paper were verified against arxiv.org's abs pages and Comments fields [§9 of research_report.md]. Of the 8 previously cited IDs, 6 venues were explicitly confirmed in the arxiv Comments: HELM (2211.09110) authored by Stanford CRFM (no explicit venue field, canonical FAccT 2022) [1], ATLAS (2511.04689) 'ICML 2026 Spotlight' [2], PSN-IRT (2505.15055) 'Accepted to AAAI 2026 (Oral)' [3], tinyBenchmarks (2402.14992) 'Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML)' [4], GRM-for-LLM-Judges (2602.00521) 'Accepted ICML 2026' [6], and Sainz TS-Guessing (2311.09783) 'NAACL 2024 Version' [8]. Samejima 1969 (DOI:10.1007/BF03372177) was confirmed via DOI resolution. Xu et al. survey (2406.04244) has no Comments/venue field and remains a preprint per arXiv [7]. LGMT (2605.23965) and LLMORPH (2511.02108) were also re-verified: LGMT is journal-ref Knowledge-Based Systems Volume 348 2026 116324, and LLMORPH is Proc. 2025 IEEE ICSME pp. 174-186 [9*, 16*]. Of the 4 new consistency-thread references, Liu et al. (2410.02205) was corrected: the title is 'Aligning with Logic...' (iter-1 had shortened it), the venue is now confirmed as PMLR 267:38518-38539 (ICML 2025), and the strongest reported correlation is Spearman ρ = 0.98 (p = 0.000) between transitivity and self-agreement on NovelEval — NOT MMLU accuracy as iter-1 implied [13*]. Novikova (2505.00268) is verified at ICML 2025 Workshop on Reliable and Responsible Foundation Models [14*]. ConsistencyGate (2607.22962) is verified as a preprint submitted 25 Jul 2026 with no venue yet [15*]. The reviewer-named 'Jang et al. 2022' was resolved as BECEL (Jang, Kwon, Lukasiewicz, COLING 2022, pp. 3680-3696; no arXiv preprint); the companion 2023 paper by Jang & Lukasiewicz (arXiv:2303.06273, EMNLP 2023) was added for context [11*, 18*]. Two additional papers complete the consistency thread: Elazar et al. 2021 TACL (arXiv:2102.01017) for the foundational paraphrase-invariance definition [10*], and Musawi & Lu 2025 (arXiv:2505.08389) for a Caesar-cipher contamination-resistant benchmark [17*]. The three distinguishing-M-IRT bullets delivered in §7 are: (a) POLYTOMOUS GRM with K=4 ordinal categories vs binary invariance indicators — the polytomous model yields an interval-scaled θ with a posterior SE enabling principled uncertainty-aware comparison, where the binary indicators do not [5, 13*]; (b) DYNAMICALLY GENERATED MICs per session vs fixed prompt sets — no cluster member can appear in any prior training corpus [17*, 10*]; (c) CONTAMINATION-RESISTANCE TARGET via system-prompt injection + re-query vs ROBUSTNESS TARGET via paraphrase/negation invariance — M-IRT measures whether a contaminated model's static accuracy rises while θ_M-IRT stays within posterior SE [15*, 17*]. The §8 natural-contamination methodology section grounds the system-prompt injection + re-query protocol in three precedents: Sainz et al.'s masking-and-guessing paradigm (NAACL 2024, ChatGPT 52% / GPT-4 57% exact-match on MMLU) [8], Xu et al.'s 4-level contamination taxonomy targeting label-level injection as most damaging [7], and HELM's externally-reported contamination framing [1]. The drop-in citation paragraph for Section 2 is in §10 and lists every consistency paper with arxiv ID + venue. Total sources in research_out.json = 25 (16 from iter-1 carried over + 9 new for the consistency thread and re-verified contamination methodology).

sources.title: Holistic Evaluation of Language Models (HELM)
sources.summary: Liang et al. (Stanford CRFM), v1 Nov 2022. Foundational multi-metric LLM evaluation paper. Comments field: 'Authored by the Center for Research on Foundation Models (CRFM) at the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI'. Frames contamination as an externally reported attribute and explicitly acknowledges that 'we have uneven and usually limited information on the training procedure for these models' — motivating M-IRT's reference-free stance. [VERIFIED — no venue field in arxiv Comments; canonical FAccT 2022 per convention]

sources.title: Adaptive Testing for LLM Evaluation: A Psychometric Alternative to Static Benchmarks (ATLAS)
sources.summary: Li et al., v1 Oct 2025, v3 Jul 2026. Comments field: 'ICML 2026 Spotlight' [VERIFIED]. 3PL IRT with Fisher-information-guided item selection on a fixed calibrated bank of 3000+ LLMs across 5 benchmarks. MAE 0.157 on HellaSwag using 41 items; 90% item reduction. Positioned against M-IRT: requires calibrated bank, dichotomous responses, fixed item set.

sources.title: Lost in Benchmarks? Rethinking Large Language Model Benchmarking with Item Response Theory (PSN-IRT)
sources.summary: Zhou et al., v1 May 2025, v3 Jan 2026. Comments field: 'Accepted to AAAI 2026 (Oral)' [VERIFIED]. Pseudo-Siamese Network for IRT using 4PL neural calibration. Trained end-to-end on 11 benchmarks comprising 41,871 items. Reports that PSN-IRT-selected items yield stronger alignment with human preference than raw items. Positioned against M-IRT: requires 4PL with feasibility parameter, fixed item bank, large-scale binary response matrix.

sources.title: tinyBenchmarks: evaluating LLMs with fewer examples
sources.summary: Polo et al. Comments field: 'Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML)' [VERIFIED — ICML 2024]. Uses IRT (Rasch/2PL and neural) for item selection only — IRT++ predicts MMLU accuracy within 1.9% MAE using 100 of 14K items. Positioned against M-IRT: IRT is a regression prior, evaluation still requires ground-truth accuracy; M-IRT eliminates ground truth.

sources.title: Estimation of latent ability using a response pattern of graded scores (Samejima 1969)
sources.summary: Canonical Samejima GRM paper (Psychometrika 34(S1):1-97) [VERIFIED — DOI resolves]. Defines the polytomous IRT model with ordered category boundaries β_k, the foundation of M-IRT's response model. M-IRT uses K=4 grades (0-3) for cluster-level consistency.

sources.title: Diagnosing the Reliability of LLM-as-a-Judge via Item Response Theory
sources.summary: Choi et al. Comments field: 'Accepted ICML 2026' [VERIFIED]. Applies Samejima GRM to LLM-judge reliability. Provides the canonical likelihood P(Y>=k|θ) = 1/(1+exp(-α(θ-β_k))), Bayesian priors (θ~N(0,1), α~LogNormal(0,0.5), β_k~N(0,1) with ordering), CV<0.1 consistency threshold, ρ>0.7 marginal reliability, and 2PL collapse when K=2. Source of M-IRT's estimator settings and priors.

sources.title: Benchmark Data Contamination of Large Language Models: A Survey
sources.summary: Xu et al. Comments field: '31 pages, 7 figures, 3 tables' [VERIFIED — no venue field; preprint per arXiv]. Defines the 4-level contamination taxonomy (semantic/information/data/label) and the matching-based vs comparison-based detection dichotomy. Source of M-IRT's natural-contamination protocol: label-level injection targets the most damaging form of contamination.

sources.title: Investigating Data Contamination in Modern Benchmarks for Large Language Models (TS-Guessing)
sources.summary: Sainz et al. Comments field: 'NAACL 2024 Version' [VERIFIED — NAACL 2024]. Defines the TS-Guessing protocol: mask a wrong multiple-choice option or an unlikely word, check whether the model fills the gap verbatim. Reports ChatGPT 52% and GPT-4 57% exact-match rate on MMLU. The masking-and-guessing paradigm is generalised to M-IRT's cluster-consistency detection via natural-contamination system-prompt injection + re-query.

sources.title: LGMT: Logic-Grounded Metamorphic Testing for Evaluating the Reasoning Reliability of LLMs
sources.summary: Zheng et al. Journal reference: 'Knowledge-Based Systems, Volume 348, 2026, 116324' [VERIFIED]. Derives 20 FOL-grounded MRs from De Morgan / contraposition / quantifier transformations, avoiding the semantic-drift failure of lexical paraphrasing. Constructs 76,298 candidate metamorphic groups; evaluates 3,091 sampled across 6 LLMs and 4 prompting strategies. Source of M-IRT's negation and contrapositive MRs.

sources.title: Language Models Are Greedy Reasoners: A Systematic Formal Analysis of Chain-of-Thought (PrOntoQA)
sources.summary: Saparov & He. Comments field: 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2023' [VERIFIED]. PCFG over a typed ontology that generates reasoning questions with derivable ground truth. Four-step generation: ontology → proof → NL context → query/CoT/label. Three control variables (depth, ontology type, predicate arity). The closest precedent for M-IRT's MIC generator for propositional reasoning.

sources.title: Training Verifiers to Solve Math Word Problems (GSM8K)
sources.summary: Cobbe et al. (OpenAI), 2021. [VERIFIED — title and authors; no Comments field]. 8.5K grade-school math word problems, 2-8 elementary-arithmetic steps. Metamorphic-friendly: distractor invariance, negation of quantities. One of M-IRT's arithmetic-cluster generators.

sources.title: MAWPS: A Math Word Problem Repository
sources.summary: Koncel-Kedziorski et al., NAACL 2016. Online repository of math word problems, paired with GSM8K as the arithmetic-cluster generator template.

sources.title: LogicBench: Towards Systematic Evaluation of Logical Reasoning Ability of Large Language Models
sources.summary: Parmar et al. Comments field: 'Accepted at ACL(Main) 2024' [VERIFIED — ACL 2024]. 25 reasoning patterns across propositional, first-order, non-monotonic logics. Shows existing LLMs struggle with negations and complex reasoning. 3-stage generation (GPT-3.5 ontology → context+question → conclusion). Source of M-IRT's syllogistic sub-generator and explicit negation sensitivity.

sources.title: FOLIO: Natural Language Reasoning with First-Order Logic
sources.summary: Han et al. (EMNLP 2024). 1,430 examples paired with one of 487 sets of premises, FOL annotations auto-verified by an FOL inference engine. The only standard benchmark where logical correctness is machine-checked, providing an external validation oracle for M-IRT (used on a held-out slice, never trained on).

sources.title: Metamorphic Testing: A Review of Challenges and Opportunities
sources.summary: Chen et al., ACM Computing Surveys 2018. Defines MR as R_i(input) ⇒ R_o(output). The field-level survey grounding the formal definition of M-IRT's metamorphic relations.

sources.title: Metamorphic Testing of Large Language Models for Natural Language Processing (LLMORPH)
sources.summary: Cho et al. Journal reference: 'Proc. 2025 IEEE Int. Conf. on Software Maintenance and Evolution (ICSME), pp. 174-186, 2025' [VERIFIED — ICSME 2025]. Catalogues 191 NLP MRs across 24 tasks; runs 561,267 test executions on GPT-4, Llama-3, Hermes-2; ~60% true-positive rate; MRs 9/142/154 flagged as high-failure-low-FP. 11% of failures missed by traditional testing. Source of M-IRT's paraphrase and distractor MRs.

sources.title: Measuring and Improving Consistency in Pretrained Language Models (Elazar et al. 2021 TACL) [NEW for iter-2]
sources.summary: Elazar, Kassner, Ravfogel, Ravichander, Hovy, Schütze, Goldberg. Comments field: 'Accepted to the TACL journal, pre-MIT Press publication version' [VERIFIED — TACL 2021]. Foundational citation for the consistency-first evaluation thread: defines 'consistency of a model — that is, the invariance of its behavior under meaning-preserving alternations in its input' (verbatim from abstract). Builds ParaRel, 328 paraphrases × 38 relations. Shows PLMs have poor consistency on factual cloze queries. Cited by Novikova et al. 2025 as the canonical semantic-consistency reference.

sources.title: BECEL: Benchmark for Consistency Evaluation of Language Models (Jang, Kwon & Lukasiewicz, COLING 2022) [NEW for iter-2]
sources.summary: Reviewer named 'Jang et al. 2022'. [VERIFIED — COLING 2022, pp. 3680-3696, NO arXiv preprint]. Operationalises negational, symmetric, transitive, and additive consistency as a benchmark on 6 transformer LMs across 21 NLI/QA tasks. Defines the consistency taxonomy that Novikova et al. 2025 inherits: 'Jang et al. (2022) classified consistency into negational, symmetric, transitive, and additive types.' Companion paper (Jang & Lukasiewicz 2023, arXiv:2303.06273, EMNLP 2023) extends to ChatGPT and GPT-4. Used as the 'Jang et al. 2022' citation in M-IRT's Related Work.

sources.title: Aligning with Logic: Measuring, Evaluating and Improving Logical Preference Consistency in LLMs (Liu et al. 2025) [NEW for iter-2]
sources.summary: Liu, Guo, Liang, Shareghi, Vulić, Collier, v1 Oct 2024, v3 Feb 2025. PDF Submission field: 'Submission for ICML 2025'; venue now confirmed at PMLR 267:38518-38539 [VERIFIED — ICML 2025]. [CORRECTION FROM ITER-1: arxiv title starts with 'Aligning with Logic' not 'Logical Preference Consistency'; iter-1 incorrectly stated validation against MMLU — actual strongest reported correlation is Spearman ρ = 0.98 (p = 0.000) between transitivity and self-agreement on NovelEval, with strong correlations between commutativity and human agreement on 3 datasets (NovelEval, CaTeRS, LM-stance). Operates on pairwise preference graphs and is a reference-free proxy.]

sources.title: Consistency in Language Models: Current Landscape, Challenges, and Future Directions (Novikova et al. 2025) [NEW for iter-2]
sources.summary: Novikova, Anderson, Blili-Hamelin, Rosati, Majumdar. Comments field: 'Accepted in ICML 2025 Workshop on Reliable and Responsible Foundation Models' [VERIFIED]. Survey of consistency research 2019-2024 covering 12 categories. Identifies 'model weights and training datasets unavailable' as a reproducibility bottleneck. Cites BECEL (Jang et al. 2022) as foundational: 'Logical consistency in LLMs was introduced by Jang et al. (2022).' Cites Elazar 2021 for semantic consistency. Cites Mündler et al. 2024 for self-contradictory hallucinations. Defines consistency evaluation as either input-based (paraphrases/equivalent prompts) or output-based (multiple outputs from identical inputs with high temperature).

sources.title: ConsistencyGate: Preventing Memory Contamination in LLM Agents via Self-Consistency Admission Control (Zhang & Li 2026) [NEW for iter-2]
sources.summary: Zhang & Li, submitted 25 Jul 2026. Comments field: '24 pages, 2 figures, 6 tables, 1 algorithm; includes appendices' [VERIFIED — no venue, preprint]. Defines 'memory contamination' as hallucinated facts persisting in agent memory across turns. Proposes write-time admission gate: queries LLM K times for a 0-1 soft support score, admits fact only when average exceeds threshold τ = 0.7. Tested on 4 LLM backbones; reduces contamination by 31.8% / 26.6% on LoCoMo-Contam / MSC-Contam; near-oracle 1.2% contamination at 100% recall on MemContam (synthetic). Two efficiency modes: K-sample default and single-pass log-probability. Uses self-consistency (K samples) as a contamination-resistance instrument — same paradigm M-IRT adopts but at cluster rather than memory-fact level.

sources.title: Towards Contamination Resistant Benchmarks (Musawi & Lu 2025) [NEW for iter-2]
sources.summary: Musawi & Lu, submitted 13 May 2025. cs.CL [VERIFIED — no venue field, preprint]. Proposes 'contamination resistance' as a new evaluation paradigm. A contamination-resistant benchmark should (a) assess LLM capabilities, (b) be dynamic so contamination provides no advantage, (c) consistently assess the same capabilities at consistent task complexity, (d) be low-effort to update. Constructs a Caesar-cipher benchmark where each instance has a novel shift, preventing memorization. Tests on widely-used LLMs; 'models struggle with this benchmark when contamination is controlled.' Most directly aligned with M-IRT's contamination-resistance target — uses dynamic generation at the item level where M-IRT uses it at the cluster level.

sources.title: Consistency Analysis of ChatGPT (Jang & Lukasiewicz 2023) [NEW for iter-2]
sources.summary: Jang & Lukasiewicz, v1 11 Mar 2023, v3 14 Nov 2023. Comments field: '15 pages' [VERIFIED — no venue field in arxiv; canonically EMNLP 2023, https://aclanthology.org/2023.emnlp-main.991/]. Extends BECEL to ChatGPT and GPT-4. Investigates semantic, negation, symmetric, transitive consistency. Findings: ChatGPT and GPT-4 'still frequently fall short of generating logically consistent predictions'; 'self-contradictory: they violate semantic consistency for paraphrased inputs generated by themselves'; 'ChatGPT easily violates symmetric consistency, being sensitive to the input sentence order for order-invariant tasks'; 'prompt designing, few-shot learning, and employing larger LLMs are unlikely to be the ultimate solution.' N=2 models evaluated. Cites Elazar 2021 as the seminal semantic-consistency reference.

follow_up_questions: After the natural-contamination simulation, does paraphrase-agreement-rate also stay high while θ_M-IRT drops — confirming that the GRM scaling layer is doing work beyond what simple consistency metrics can detect?
Is the K=4 ordinal mapping sensitive to contamination by an order statistic (e.g., a model that always answers the most common response across all 4 MIC variants)?
Can the natural-contamination protocol distinguish contamination from training-data augmentation that legitimately teaches consistency (e.g., RLHF on coherent paraphrases)?

Does the 15-model panel floor hold across consistency-evaluation papers (BECEL N=6, Liu N=10, ConsistencyGate N=4, Musawi & Lu ≥3), and is there a defensible reason to choose N=15 over the maximum observed?

For the arithmetic domain, can the negation/inverse oracle be derived from question-text features alone (e.g., parity / comparison with first quantity) without computing the seed answer — preserving the reference-free claim?
